findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. They can say what it is and why it matters before they scroll.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable.

findings.text: Someone arriving at Athena's own site finds a page that is almost all about a different project, firstmate. The second and third paragraphs explain why, but only the opening paragraph is about Athena itself.
There is a link to next steps near the top, and the Next steps section gives prerequisites, a clone command, an install command and a one-line first try. The reader knows what to do next.
findings.source: Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself

findings.text: The clone step is followed directly by `./setup.sh` with no step to change into the cloned folder. A newcomer who copies the commands in order runs setup from the wrong directory.
This link sits in the header with no explanation. A newcomer is not an owner, has no proposals and cannot tell what the link is for.
findings.source: Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision.

findings.text: The Start here section explains firstmate plainly and follows one task from start to finish. It shows clearly what an Athena study is like.
findings.source: Firstmate is a tool for people who direct AI coding agents. It keeps a backlog of programming tasks and hands each one to a worker...

findings.text: Terms are defined twice, word for word in places: for example, 'in scope' and 'red' match in both lists. This makes a long, dense page longer, and some terms are used before they are defined (the 'local-only landing' entry uses 'ship' before the page explains it).
Claim c37 says 'the main first mate', a term the page never defines or uses anywhere else. A newcomer cannot tell how it relates to firstmate or the agent.
findings.source: which stays with the main first mate

findings.text: This finding is about paths missed on the first reading, but it carries the same 'not run' tag as f1. That label fits only its last sentence, so the reader is left unsure what the tag means.
findings.source: f3 not run A first reading of the pinned tree missed these paths

findings.text: The citation scheme is explained up front, and every claim links to exact lines at a pinned commit. This supports the page's point that Athena's output can be traced.
findings.source: Each statement below ends with the id of the claim that supports it; the claims, with links to their sources, are listed at the end.
